messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the RFC yesterday — can we land on a 'qualifier' shim to resolve routing ties (region vs cost vs latency)? thinking lightweight and runtime-friendly, not another full plugin.

alex: +1 to a shim. we need to be explicit about precedence and whether qualifiers are deterministic or probabilistic. deterministic = easier to debug, probabilistic helps load distribution.

sam: cost: probabilistic adds instrumentation/telemetry complexity. runtime-wise deterministic is cheaper (single compare) but may cause hot shards. we should allow a tie-breaker weight with decay.

maria: thinking: qualifier = small JSON object on route decisions, e.g. `{\"priority\": \"latency\", \"bias\": 0.15}` that runtime applies after primary policy. simple semantics: bias in [-1,1], positive favors primary, negative favors fallback.

tasha: can we keep this as an opt-in feature per-tenant? ops + SRE will want rollout gates. also need clear observability: which qualifier ran and effective score delta.

alex: telemetry: emit `route.qualifier.{tenant}.{qualifier_id}.delta` and a boolean `route.qualifier.applied`. Also add a histogram for post-qualifier latency/cost so we can A/B.

maria: good. runtime contract: qualifier must be pure (no external calls), idempotent, and run within decision budget (<= 200us). otherwise we invalidate and fallback to primary.

sam: implementation idea: two-tier evaluation — 1) compile-time validate qualifier DSL (compact), 2) runtime VM (tiny stack) or native evaluator for hot paths. prefer native for common ops (add, mul, weight).

alex: compat question: if we roll out qualifiers, what happens when policies compiled without qualifiers hit a runtime that expects them? should be backward compatible — runtime treats missing qualifier as neutral.

maria: yes neutral by default. also add a version field on qualifier so we can deprecate older semantics.

tasha: rollout plan: feature-flagged in control-plane UI, default off for tenants. 1) enable in staging+canary tenants, collect metrics for 48h, 2) enable in low-traffic production tenants, 3) open opt-in to users. Document fallback behavior.

sam: tests: unit for evaluator, e2e sim harness feed with realistic distribution (latency/cost) to confirm no spike in hot shards. add chaos test where qualifier throws to ensure neutral fallback.

alex: ops-wise, we should add an alert: `route.qualifier.applied_rate` deviates > 10% from sim baseline. also watch `route.rejections` for time budget failures.

maria: config example for RFC notes (small):
```
{
  "qualifier_id": "latency_bias_v1",
  "version": 1,
  "expr": "score + bias * (region_pref - cost_norm)",
  "params": {"bias": 0.12}
}
```

maria: question for infra: is the sidecar path viable or should we host qualifier in central router?

sam: sidecar = lower latency to tenant signals and easier canary per-tenant, but harder to ship compiled validators. central router = easier to maintain and global view for probes but could be a bottleneck. personally prefer sidecar for first pass.

tasha: sidecar rollout is more operational work but buys per-tenant isolation. if we start sidecar-only, we must ensure fallback to central router for older versions.

alex: agreement: start sidecar implementation behind feature flag. add compiler in control-plane to validate DSL and emit bytecode for sidecar. central router should accept neutral/no-qualifier.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: link to workspace: https://redwood-infra/policies/qualifier-shim (staging diff posted) :rocket:

maria: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with config schema, telemetry names, and rollout steps. @alex @sam can you sketch evaluator micro-benchmarks (latency/cpu) by EOD? @tasha please add ops checklist.

alex: on it, will post numbers.

sam: I can prototype the native evaluator and run bench.

tasha: adding checklist now, will include migration playbook and alerting rules.

maria: thanks — if we get the telemetry right we can iterate biases without surprises. :thumbsup:
